Twelve comments

Waterford waltz

Nice one, Tusong. I’m not a great fan of waltzes but have always liked this one.

↳ Posted by Kenny on March 4th, 2004.

This is in one of the O‘Farrell books, printed in the first decade of the 19th century. I’ve a tape of Waterford piper Tommy Kearney playing it; as in O’Farrell’s setting it has another part that goes up to high D, in the third octave. A beautiful tune; where’d it come from?

↳ Posted by Lucy Rietmann on March 11th, 2004.

Waterford Waltz

X:5 from O‘Farrell’s. Barlines connected, and the run up to d’ shows up - the high notes don’t in ceolachan’s contributions for some reason. This is as Tommy Kearney and Mick O’Brien play it on recordings, too.

↳ Posted by Lucy Rietmann on November 16th, 2013.

Re: Waterford

This might sound a bit odd but…I can’t help feeling that this does in some ways have the feel of a mazurka? Sort of similar in some way, at least to me, to the third part of Sonny Brogan’s mazurka? Probably just me I guess. Have to admit I didn’t know of or can’t remember hearing this tune before so it’s nice to come across it now.

↳ Posted by john knoss on November 2nd, 2023.

Tricky 3rd part but it’s a lovely tune
